title: Cold-path profiling: weekly lab digest
content:
Summary:

This digest captures the week’s focused investigation into cold-path tail latency and throughput regression signals we started seeing in the mid-August spike. The goal for this sprint was to reproduce a representative cold-start scenario, isolate the dominant latency contributors (kernel selection, NVMe paging, cuda context priming, kv-cache miss handling), and validate a low-risk mitigation we can A/B in shadow runs.

Key outcomes (TL;DR):
- Reproduced p99 cold-start spikes locally and in the lab (config: g5.12xlarge equivalent, batch=1, seq=1024, half precision). p99 initial response increased from ~210ms baseline to ~1.8s in high-pressure runs.
- Root contributors identified: NVMe-backed kv cache miss path (serialization + disk read) and delayed CUDA context warmup on GPU reset boundaries.
- Lightweight mitigation: eager cudaContextCreate at instance startup + nonblocking prefetch for top-1 prefix reduces p99 cold from ~1.8s to ~420ms in our lab runs.
- Next steps: sequence of canary shadow runs (prod-mirrors) + a small infra rollback plan if OOM or tail regressions reappear.

Background and motivation:
We observed intermittent production reports of slow first-token latency for certain customer routes (batch=1, few-shot prompts, long seq). These were correlated with long periods of low traffic followed by sudden bursts. The serving-runtime has multiple cold paths: a) kernel selection & JIT/compilation, b) kv-cache miss requiring NVMe read path, c) CUDA context (driver vs container) warmup when GPU is reclaimed, d) model weight page-in for recycled pods. The lab goal this week was to stress these paths in isolation where possible.

Experiment matrix (runs executed):
- Run A: baseline warm-run (control) — steady qps 80, no pod recycle, batch=4, seq=256. (used to sanity-check runner)
- Run B: cold-start synthetic — simulate pod spin from idle: start process, first request only, batch=1, seq=1024, prompt len=512, repeat 200 samples with 10s idle gap between groups.
- Run C: nvme-heavy — pre-populate large kv index, then evict prefix cache, trigger first requests to force NVMe read path.
- Run D: cuda-reset — force GPU context teardown between requests (mimic preemption), measure time to first-forward and kernel launch times.
- Run E: mitigation trial — eager context create + async prefetch for top prefix + reduced compile-logging.

Raw metrics highlights (lab median / p95 / p99):
- Run B (cold-start synthetic): median 320ms / p95 780ms / p99 1800ms
- Run C (nvme-heavy): median 410ms / p95 930ms / p99 1650ms (disk read spikes line up with p99)
- Run D (cuda-reset): median 290ms / p95 640ms / p99 1400ms (observed extra 250–350ms during driver initialization)
- Run E (mitigated): median 210ms / p95 330ms / p99 420ms

Profiling notes:
- Flamegraphs captured via eBPF and nvprof for samples in Run C show a significant block time inside nvme_read_async -> serializer (Python layer) where the event loop waits for io completion.
- CUDA trace shows that context creation is a nontrivial part of the 2nd component of cold latency; enabling persistent context reduces that phase.
- Kernel selection/compile time is small for the model variant used (no JIT happened during these runs), but we saw sporadic small spikes tied to un-cached kernel lookups for unusual seq lengths.

Hypotheses and evidence: (ranked)
1) NVMe kv-cache miss path is the dominant contributor to p99 during cold reads (evidence: synchronous disk read timing aligned with p99; Run C improved when cache warmed).
2) CUDA context recreation contributes a stable ~200–350ms overhead on cold starts (evidence: Run D timing, and mitigation reducing that window).
3) Rare kernel lookup misses add 50–150ms spikes for unusual seq combos (evidence: traces from ~3 samples across different runs).

Low-risk mitigation tried this week (details):
- Implementation: on worker process start, call cudaSetDevice + cudaDeviceSynchronize to precreate the context (non-blocking for request threads). Add an async prefetch path: for the last-used top-1 prefix (heuristic) issue an nvme read into DRAM using aio in a background thread.
- Observed: p99 dropped from 1800ms to 420ms in lab, no increase in steady-state p50/p95, and memory overhead within expected margins (+~120MB per worker).
- Caveats: background prefetch increases transient memory footprint; for memory-constrained nodes we must gate prefetch under a toggle.

Risks and rollbacks:
- OOM risk if many workers prefetch large prefixes concurrently. Mitigation: add a global prefetch token bucket (configurable), max-prefetch-per-instance, and prefetch-size cap.
- Potential for masking deeper NVMe throughput issues; if we prefetch too aggressively, we may create steady high IO. Plan to monitor iostat and node-level io wait during shadow.

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Priya: implement prefetch token-bucket + config flags for prefetch size & concurrency. ETA: 2026-10-05.
- Liang: add persistent cuda context flag behind feature-flag + unit tests. ETA: 2026-10-03.
- Maya: run prod-mirror shadow run (region: us-west-2) with mitigation toggled on 10% of nodes, collect p50/p95/p99, iostat, gpu-mem footprint. ETA: 2026-10-07.
- Rafael: create dashboard panels (probe: cold-start-first-token) and alert when p99 > 600ms for >5m sustained in canary. ETA: 2026-10-04.
- Ethan (owner): coordinate post-shadow retro and prepare rollout plan for Dedicated customers with opt-in knob. ETA: 2026-10-12.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How will this interact with Dedicated nodes where customers pin models and have constrained memory footprints? We need to run a replica test with Dedicated config.
- Are there any eco-system side effects for long-lived pre-created CUDA contexts (driver version edge-cases)? Need SRE/infra signoff.
- Is our heuristic for top-1 prefix prefetch good enough for multi-tenant hosts? Might pollute host memory for many small tenants.

Meeting notes (2026-09-29 10:30 AM PT, 40m):
Attendees: Ethan, Priya, Liang, Maya, Rafael, Helen (SRE brief sync)
- Quick recap of week’s runs and the mitigation numbers.
- Helen: asked to validate iostat and per-disk queue depths during shadow; offered to run node-level collection for the 10% canary.
- Decision: proceed with limited shadow in us-west-2 with prefetch gated to 10 tokens per node; enable persistent-cuda-flag behind ff.
- Agreed to hold rollout for Dedicated until we have memory guardrails and a small Dedicated-run test.

Notes to reviewers:
- The lab runs were deterministic with our harness v2.1 (link in linked_artifacts). Reproduction scripts: run_cold_harness.sh in the serving-runtime repo (PR linked).
- Please review prefetch caps carefully (Priya’s PR will contain initial defaults). We should be conservative for the first shadow.

Appendix — quick commands & reproducer pointers:
- Local reproducer: scripts/perf/cold_repro.sh --batch 1 --seq 1024 --samples 200
- Capture traces: tools/trace_collect.sh --type eBPF --out traces/2026-09-29
- Relevant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1024
- JIRA: PERF-4387 (cold-path profiling and mitigation)

Next sync: 2026-10-06 10:30 AM PT — plan to review shadow metrics and decide on broader rollout.

End of digest.
